text:
maria: Quick flag: we see progressive token-level hallucination on long-context workloads when using post-layer int4 profiles. Repro below, pinging @alex @li for design tradeoff brainstorm.

alex: can you summarize metrics & minimal repro?

maria: repro: run longform-summary suite (~1200 tokens) with profile `postnorm-int4-v2`. Observed drift: entropy collapse after ~700 tokens, repeated phrases increase. sample diffs: ent -0.6, token_repeat_rate 0.38 vs fp16 0.09, ROUGE-L -4.5. Minimal steps:

```
# create profile
calibrate(model, mode='postnorm', bits=4, per_channel=false, samples=150)
# inference
infer(model_quant, dataset='longform_summary')
```

li: interesting. could be quantization bias accumulating across residual connections. Any layer-level stat that points to drift?

maria: yes: layer residual mean slowly shifts positive across layers (0.005 -> 0.042). hypothesis: folding bias terms before quantization + asymmetric quant scale causes systematic offset. Not the same as headwise clipping seen earlier.

dmitri: rollout options: 1) retrain/calibrate with bias-correction during quantization 2) runtime correction shim that subtracts learned float offset after dequantize 3) route long requests to int8/fp8. Tradeoffs?

alex: retraining/calibrate is expensive operationally for every profile tweak. runtime shim seems cheap if we store per-layer float vectors. Need to measure perf: extra vector add per transformer block, should be memory-bound but small.

maria: prototype idea: for each transformer block store a float32 offset vector (length = hidden_dim). At runtime after dequantize do: out = deq_out - offset. Offsets learned on small calibration set; store in profile blob. Controls: apply_threshold_by_layer_energy, max_abs_offset cap.

li: add telemetry: `quant_offset_mean[layer]`, `quant_offset_l2[layer]`, and request-level `longctx_quality_delta` comparing shadow FP path. If offset mean > 0.03 or l2 > 0.1 -> auto-failover to int8.

dmitri: we should also implement a shadowing canary: for 2% of long requests mirror both shimmed-int4 and baseline-fp16 (no extra latency) and compute quality delta. Canary-bot schedule?

canary-bot: Scheduled: shadow-int4-offset-shim on prod-dedicated @ 05/01 02:00 UTC (2% mirror sample)

alex: lifecycle: offsets must be versioned and invalidated on model/weight updates. Add `offset_version` and `offset_created_at` to profile metadata and a lint that prevents enabling shim without offsets. Also allow customer override to force route to safer precision.

maria: safety rules: require min_layer_energy >= 5e-4 before applying offset for that layer; also clamp offsets to +-0.05 to avoid over-correction. If any layer hits clamp frequently, mark profile degraded.

li: tests: synthetic accumulation test generating steady residual bias across many tokens to ensure shim stabilizes distribution and doesn't introduce oscillation. Also perf smoke that measures throughput delta (<2% expected).

alex: ops alerts: create alert if `shadow_longctx_delta > 0.03` for 5m or `offset_age > 24h`. Also dashboard showing per-layer offset histograms.

maria: action items: maria -> implement shim + unit + synthetic test; li -> canary config + shadow metrics; alex -> telemetry + alerts + lint rule. ETA: 1 week.

dmitri: one more thought: for models with narrow hidden sizes, offsets may be noisy; treat small layers as skip (configurable).

maria: noted. will include `min_hidden_dim=512` gate. Thanks all. Filing RFC follow-up with playbook and rollback steps.
